2607.21636.title: Measuring the Dependency Gap: Diagnosing Inter-Column Fidelity in Tabular Generative Models
2607.21636.paper_summary: Synthetic tabular data is prized for preserving not just each column's marginal distribution but the dependencies between columns - structure that carries much of the discriminative signal for minority classes in imbalanced domains such as fraud detection and clinical risk. Yet the metrics most commonly used to certify such data are largely blind to this structure: a fully-factorized baseline that destroys all inter-column dependency is judged nearly indistinguishable from real data by the logistic-regression C2ST, while the pairwise Trend score is only partially sensitive. We introduce a dependency-aware fidelity diagnostic that decomposes a strong gradient-boosted classifier two-sample test (XGB-C2ST) into marginal, dependency, and numerical-categorical cross components, anchored between a fully-factorized lower bound and a real-data oracle upper bound. Applying it to state-of-the-art flow-matching (TabbyFlow/EF-VFM) and diffusion (TabDiff) generators, we expose a real dependency gap that standard metrics miss and that tracks minority-class utility. The gap is not a structural limitation of mean-field objectives - consistent with recent recovery results, these are asymptotically exact - yet it is stubborn: neither a 16x capacity increase nor post-hoc copula correction closes it, pointing to the absence of direct dependency supervision rather than a capacity or structural limit.
2607.21636.paper_summary_zh: 合成表格數據因為能夠保留每一列的邊際分佈以及列之間的依賴性而受到重視——這種結構承載了在不平衡領域（如詐騙檢測和臨床風險）中少數類別的重要判別信號。 然而，目前用來認證這類數據的指標在很大程度上對這種結構視而不見：一個完全分解的基線摧毀了所有列間依賴性，並被邏輯回歸C2ST評價為幾乎無法與真實數據區分，而成對的趨勢分數則只有部分敏感性。我們引入了一種依賴性意識的忠實度診斷，將強梯度提升分類器的兩樣本測試（XGB-C2ST）分解為邊際、依賴性和數值-類別交叉組件，並固定在完全分解的下界和真實數據的上界之間。將其應用於最先進的流匹配（TabbyFlow/EF-VFM）和擴散（TabDiff）生成器，我們揭示了一個標準指標所忽視的真實依賴性差距，並且該差距跟踪少數類別的效用。這個差距並不是均場目標的結構性限制——與最近的恢復結果一致，這些結果是漸近精確的——但它是頑固的：無論是16倍的容量增加還是事後的copula校正都無法縮小這個差距，這指向缺乏直接的依賴性監督，而不是容量或結構的限制。
2607.21636.author: Jie Zhang et.al.
